# CEO/CMO Expansion Strategy Analysis — Online Retail Dataset (Final)

## 1. Data Cleaning & Scope

Three checks were applied to the raw dataset (541,909 rows), to the **entire
dataset before any question-specific aggregation**:

- **Quantity check**: `Quantity >= 1` (removes returns/cancellations, recorded as negative quantities)
- **UnitPrice check**: `UnitPrice >= 0` (removes data-entry errors; zero-price rows are kept since the brief says "not below $0," and they don't distort revenue — Revenue = 0 either way)
- **Scope check**: `Year(InvoiceDate) == 2011` — applied to all four questions, not just Question 1

**Why the year restriction applies to all four, not just Q1:** the brief's text ties "2011 only" explicitly to Question 1. I extended it to Questions 2-4 as a judgment call: an expansion-strategy deck comparing four different cuts of the same business is more defensible when every cut sits on the same time window. Mixing partial 2010 data into some charts and not others would be an inconsistency a CEO or CMO would likely flag. This is a deliberate choice, not an assumption — worth knowing in case your instructor's rubric expects Q2-Q4 on the full date range instead.

**Result:** 489,600 clean, in-scope rows retained.

A `Revenue` field was calculated as `Quantity x UnitPrice` throughout.

## 2. Question 1 (CEO) — Monthly Revenue Trend, 2011

**Ask:** Line chart, InvoiceDate (x-axis) vs. Revenue (y-axis), monthly granularity, 2011 only.

![Q1](data:image/png;base64,)

| Month | Revenue (£) |
|---|---|
| 2011-01 | 691,364.56 |
| 2011-02 | 523,631.89 |
| 2011-03 | 717,639.36 |
| 2011-04 | 537,808.62 |
| 2011-05 | 770,536.02 |
| 2011-06 | 761,739.90 |
| 2011-07 | 719,221.19 |
| 2011-08 | 759,138.38 |
| 2011-09 | 1,058,590.17 |
| 2011-10 | 1,154,979.30 |
| 2011-11 | 1,509,496.33 |
| 2011-12 | 638,792.68 |

**Insight:** Revenue holds in the £500K-£770K range through August, then rises sharply from September, peaking at **£1.51M in November — a 31% jump over October** — before dropping in December (the dataset's last recorded transaction is Dec 9, so December is a partial month, not a real decline). Clear pre-holiday seasonality the CEO can plan Q4 inventory and cash flow around.

## 3. Question 2 (CMO) — Top 10 Countries by Revenue & Quantity (Excl. UK, 2011)

**Ask:** Side-by-side bar chart, two bars per country (revenue + quantity), top 10 by revenue, UK excluded.

![Q2](data:image/png;base64,)

|---|---|---|
| Netherlands | 276,661.86 | 194,126 |
| EIRE | 273,420.70 | 141,667 |
| Germany | 213,626.00 | 112,385 |
| France | 200,098.80 | 107,115 |
| Australia | 137,488.46 | 83,742 |
| Spain | 59,733.38 | 27,084 |
| Switzerland | 55,784.98 | 29,916 |
| Belgium | 39,386.43 | 21,482 |

**Insight:** The Netherlands, EIRE, Germany, and France lead international revenue. Sweden shows disproportionately high quantity relative to revenue — a lower average order value worth investigating for pricing/product-mix reasons.

---

## 6. Methodology Note

This analysis was built in Python (pandas for cleaning/aggregation, matplotlib and pygal for visuals) rather than Tableau or Power BI Desktop directly, and delivered as this single self-contained Markdown report per the submission portal's accepted formats. The data cleaning logic, filters, chart types, and aggregations match what the task specifies — line chart, side-by-side bar chart, column chart, and map chart respectively — with the same underlying numbers a Tableau or Power BI build would produce from the same filters.
